policy.name: code-intel-integration-orchestration
policy.rule: Normal code-intel runs must use integrations registered here. Separately installed project-intelligence CLIs are allowed only as compatibility shims or optional accelerators.
policy.extensionRule: Add new projects, scanners, memory systems, graph providers, or governance strategies here before wiring them into pipeline scripts.

stages.description: Resolve repo path and verify runtime plus registered integration contracts.
Compiled Rust command and worker targets used by the pipeline.
Exact repo file and text surface.
Optional, non-blocking long-term project memory, index, status, and docs; included in the default plan when available.
Architecture graph snapshot and graph freshness.
Structural scan, rules, gate, DSM, evolution, and what-if signals.
Hotspot and reference localization for agents.
Reduced or full repository orientation assembled from snapshot-bound evidence.
Hospital diagnosis, next protocol, and surgery-plan routing.
Implementation-independent behavioral specs, test vectors, acceptance criteria, and provenance.
Content-bound measurement and approval gates without mutation authority.
Atomic run publication after artifact validation and before index admission.
Durable artifact index for later sessions.

integrations.extensionPoint: The probe is native Rust (doctor_bootstrap.rs) and stays an observation-only bootstrap. Authoritative doctor execution uses the A01 envelope and never promotes readiness into conformance or admissibility.
Integration orchestration plus artifact resume/classify behavior belongs in this Rust binary.
C00 owns necessity and first-sufficient admission only; product priority and code-style policy remain out of scope.
VCS providers may replace discovery only by preserving the versioned portable identity and overlay contract.
Provider adapters emit this port contract; provider-specific logic must not enter the admissibility core.
Repowise remains external; this adapter translates native observations and submits every emitted evidence request through A04 before any downstream consumer may use it.

The adapter is the only admissible architecture-graph evidence route. Internal Rust and explicit Understand-compatible fallback outputs must preserve this port and pass A04; direct graph artifacts are not current anatomy.

The default native provider executes gate/check with independently approved admission policy and typed results, preserving DR-0011 measurement and normalizing observations through A04. External providers without a valid same-policy handshake remain unknown for admission. Diagnosis policy stays in Hospital.

Explicit, optional CodeGraph provider for the code/Git perception layer. Rust owns scope, snapshot binding, artifacts, admission and failure semantics; CodeGraph retains parsing, resolution, storage and ranking. No shared SQLite or codenexus.full impersonation. Partial semantic coverage remains advisory/unknown and cannot replace native evidence or authoritative gates.

Mindwalk extraction remains optional and replaceable. Code Intel owns path safety, privacy reduction, snapshot binding, structural joins, and advisory review semantics; no raw provider content gains gate or fact authority.

Full CodeNexus and explicit lite compatibility output share this adapter and A04 route. CodeNexus retains process, storage, retrieval, and impact semantics; absence remains provider-unavailable/unknown without fabricated facts. The builtin lite-compat implementation is a DAG caller (evidence.codenexus) that generates the context in-process.

B05 composes A01/A02/A03/A04 evidence only. It may add basic repository identity or inventory observations, but deeper structural intelligence remains provider-owned and must stay unknown while CodeNexus is unavailable.
D01 composes verified evidence only. Purpose remains unknown without admitted purpose evidence; deeper architecture and semantic models remain outside this atom.

D03 projects D01 claims into a deterministic criticality x confidence view. C01 Method Cards and C02 selection may consume the projection but cannot be supplied as classification inputs or rewrite its provenance, scores, or quadrant.
D02 measures D01 without changing orientation semantics. A fast result without complete claim provenance is rejected; clean-machine repetition remains an independent verification condition.

D04 derives observed baseline/current/delta value-stream and predecessor-closed critical-path measurements from A07-committed local opt-in events. It cannot create schedule or staffing commitments, and mandatory verification is protected from waste attribution.
OpenSpec OPSX, spec-kit, gstack, matt-flow, and BMAD remain candidates. This atom emits proposals only; A05 authority is required before adoption, initialization, or execution.

The catalog binds external agent assets by reference; nothing is vendored into this repository. Candidates carry a committed fit, license, security, integration, and reversibility rating, and this atom emits proposals only; A05 authority is required before adoption, installation, or execution. Adding a candidate means adding a catalog entry, not a runtime branch.
C06 owns correlation and fail-closed request/response validation only. UI, chat, tmux, brokers, authority adoption, and durable C07 records remain outside the port.
C07 owns additive durable resolution and replay only. C06 remains the request transport; changed snapshots, changed evidence, and expired evidence reopen the gap.
A07 consumes a fully validated A09 manifest and A06-restaged refs. It owns publication only; A08 index admission remains separate.

Run profiles compile into one immutable ExecutionPolicy. Capability adapters execute behind A01 envelopes; the private controller alone binds repository.iteration provenance to the run, snapshot, repository key, and publication name before marker-last publication.
Capability executors remain behind A01 envelopes; the coordinator has no provider or tool authority. Seeded diagnosis accepts only A03-verified, current-snapshot A04 admission Artifact Refs.
Add inventory engines behind this adapter; do not call new inventory CLIs directly from agents.

Built-in deterministic baseline only. Parser coverage is heuristic and relationship/call-graph precision remains explicit unknown; external cocoindex and specialized semantic graphs stay separate adapters.
Preview-only structural search and rewrite planning through ast-grep. Repository mutation is deliberately excluded and requires a separate explicitly authorized capability.

Advisory-only structural security scan through a bundled, originally-authored per-language ast-grep rule set (orchestration/ast-grep-rules/). Never proposes a rewrite, never gates get_gate_verdict; findings are review prompts, not verified vulnerabilities.

The only capability in this registry that rewrites repository source bytes. It writes exactly the addressed spans of exactly one file, after verifying each span's current bytes against a caller-supplied sha256, and publishes the expected/found digests as evidence when it refuses. Structural planning stays in edit.ast-grep-plan; this capability never decides what to change.

This command is the preferred native producer behind provider.graph-adapt. Its direct artifact is not admissible current anatomy until the adapter binds it to the requested snapshot and A04 accepts it.

Use only as an explicitly selected fallback or legacy rollback. Output must enter provider.graph-adapt with a named fallback identity and pass A04; direct external artifacts never become current anatomy.
External sentrux.exe is an optional accelerator behind provider.sentrux-adapt; neither direct output is diagnosis authority before A04.
This adapter is non-blocking and replaceable; Survival Scanner preserves localization when it is unavailable. Full CodeNexus backends must adapt to codenexus-context.json before replacing it.
B09 consumes only A04 admission Artifact Refs. Markdown and surgery-plan Markdown are rebuildable views and never diagnosis authority.

Routing is deterministic and side-effect free. A discovered or authenticated channel never implies consumption, external-egress, or paid-spend authorization; pinned adapters do not fall back unless policy explicitly allows it.
Pipeline-owned, optional, local read-only evidence. AIGX may be an upstream translator but is never a runtime dependency or trust bypass.
Explicit local JSON only. Missing, partial, stale, snapshot-mismatched, or unobserved evidence remains unknown and cannot become green.

A08 is a rebuildable materialized view and never run authority. Normal admission requires an A07 marker plus exactly one verified repository.iteration provenance Artifact Ref whose run, snapshot, repository, and publication bindings match the authority path; legacy traversal is explicit compatibility only.

Rust owns snapshot binding, method-catalog and committed-artifact reads, candidate validation, and staged advisory publication. Agent-authored text remains advisory and never grants promotion, commit, issue, or plan approval authority; network and repository mutation are outside this capability.
